title: Independent UK test of eight mammography AI algorithms as second reader and triage
summary: Eight commercial deep learning breast cancer detection algorithms from five vendors were evaluated retrospectively on 22,778 mammograms from two UK screening sites (Cambridge, Norwich; 2017) with 3-year follow-up. Standalone AUCs ranged 0.82-0.91, with one algorithm inferior to all others. Paired with the first human reader, all but one were noninferior in sensitivity to double reading (64.7-67.4% vs 67.9%) with superior specificity (97.5% vs 97.1%); low-suspicion triage ruled out 37.4-65.7% of mammograms while missing at most 1.0% of screen-detected cancers. Gains came with more arbitration, and the study is retrospective; prospective workflow effects were not measured.
ai_technology: Commercial deep learning breast cancer detection algorithms scoring digital screening mammograms.

evidence.tested: Retrospective evaluation on 22,778 UK screening mammograms with histopathology-confirmed screen-detected, interval and next-round cancers; noninferiority at a 5% margin.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance, effects on reader behaviour and arbitration workload in practice, generalisability beyond two 2017 UK sites; vendor-level results and full methods not reviewed (full text not accessed).
evidence.ai_role: The deep learning algorithms produced the cancer suspicion scores whose standalone, paired-reader and triage performance is the finding.

source_review.scope: Independent review: structured abstract from Europe PMC, Crossref dates, OpenAlex affiliations. Springer full text not read.
